title: Neuro Emergencies: Stroke, Seizure, Brain Pressure

questions.stem: A client with a head injury is becoming restless and confused. Vital signs are normal. What is this most likely?

options.text: A late sign of rising brain pressure
The earliest sign of rising brain pressure

questions.explanation: B is correct: the earliest sign of rising brain pressure is a change in level of consciousness, like restlessness or confusion; don't wait for the vital signs to change. A, late signs, involve vital sign changes. C dismisses it. D isn't supported by the stem.

questions.stem: Which are late signs of rising brain pressure? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: late signs are rising blood pressure, a slow pulse, and irregular breathing, called Cushing's triad. D and E are early signs.

questions.stem: Which position is correct for a client at risk for rising brain pressure?

options.text: Head of bed at 30 degrees, head straight
Head of bed at 90 degrees, head turned

questions.explanation: B is correct: keep the head of the bed at 30 degrees and the head straight. A, C, and D are not the taught position.

questions.stem: What does BE FAST stand for in stroke recognition? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, C, D, and E are correct: BE FAST is balance, eyes, face drooping, arm weakness, speech trouble, and time to call. F, fever, is not part of it.

questions.stem: A client with stroke symptoms arrives. Which test comes first, and why?

options.text: Blood sugar, to rule out a seizure
A brain scan, to tell a clot from a bleed
A swallow test, to allow medications
A chest X-ray, to rule out a lung problem

questions.explanation: B is correct: a brain scan comes first to tell a clot from a bleed, because clot-busting drugs could make a bleed worse. A, C, and D are not the first step taught.

questions.stem: A client with a new stroke asks for water. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Give nothing by mouth until a swallow screen

questions.explanation: B is correct: give nothing by mouth until a swallow screen. A, C, and D give fluids before the screen.

questions.stem: A client starts having a seizure in bed. What is the first action?

options.text: Put a padded tongue blade in the mouth
Hold the arms and legs still
Turn the client on their side and time the seizure

questions.explanation: C is correct: turn the client on their side and time the seizure. A, never put anything in the mouth. B, never restrain. D, stay with the client.

questions.stem: Which actions are correct during a seizure? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct: time it, protect the head, and loosen tight clothing. D and E are never done.

questions.stem: A client's seizure has lasted 6 minutes. What does this mean?

options.text: It is a normal seizure length

questions.explanation: B is correct: a seizure lasting over 5 minutes is an emergency, and 6 minutes is over 5. A, C, and D downplay it.

questions.stem: A client admitted after a stroke is being monitored for rising pressure in the brain. Which finding is an early sign?
questions.explanation: B is correct: early signs of rising brain pressure are restlessness, confusion, headache, and being harder to wake. A, fixed pupils, C, a slow pulse, and D, irregular breathing, are late signs.
